name: Example: AI policy for a regulated retail bank
description: Illustrative organisation policy showing how a regulated firm tightens the default: customer-facing AI is high risk, the financial threshold drops to 250, a model-risk validation control is added, and the high tier requires a larger golden set. Place it at .ai-governance/policy.json in a workspace.

autonomy_levels.name: Inform
autonomy_levels.description: The AI surfaces information; a human decides everything.

autonomy_levels.name: Suggest
autonomy_levels.description: The AI proposes options; a human chooses.

autonomy_levels.name: Draft
autonomy_levels.description: The AI produces a complete draft; a human reviews, edits and sends it.

autonomy_levels.name: Act with approval
autonomy_levels.description: The AI prepares an action; a human approves each action before it runs.

autonomy_levels.name: Act and report
autonomy_levels.description: The AI acts, then reports with an undo window; a human monitors and can reverse.

autonomy_levels.name: Autonomous
autonomy_levels.description: The AI acts without review of individual actions; humans audit samples and metrics.

tiers.name: Minimal
tiers.description: Internal, assistive use with no personal data beyond business contact details.

tiers.name: Limited
tiers.description: Customer-facing or externally published output, personal data, data shared with an external model provider, or hard-to-reverse actions.

tiers.name: High
tiers.description: Influences decisions about people's access to jobs, credit, insurance, housing, education, healthcare or essential services; sensitive data; regulated advice; children or vulnerable users; high-value or autonomous actions affecting customers.

tiers.name: Prohibited
tiers.description: Practices this organisation does not build or buy. Stop the work; there is no approval path.

questions.text: Will people outside the organisation see the AI's output or interact with it directly?
Will AI-generated content be published externally under the organisation's name (marketing, documentation, social media)?
Does the system process personal data beyond business contact details?
Does it process sensitive data: health, biometric, genetic, financial account, government ID, criminal record, or data about children?
Does the output influence decisions about people's access to employment, credit, insurance, housing, education, healthcare, legal or other essential services?
Does it give or support regulated advice (medical, legal, financial, tax) or run inside a regulated process?
Are children or other vulnerable groups likely to be users or subjects?
Will confidential or personal data be sent to an external model provider?
Does the system retrieve internal documents or records to ground its answers (RAG)?
Can the system call tools that change state, such as sending messages, updating records, paying or deleting?
Can any of those actions be hard or impossible to reverse?
What is the highest autonomy level planned (L0 Inform to L5 Autonomous)?
What is the largest direct financial impact of a single AI output or action, in the reporting currency? Use 0 if none.
Does the system use any of these practices? Select every one that applies, or 'none'.

rules.reason: Uses a practice this organisation prohibits.
Influences decisions about people's access to important opportunities or services.
Gives or supports regulated advice, or runs inside a regulated process.
Children or vulnerable people are likely users or subjects.
A single output or action can have a direct financial impact of 250 or more.
Acts without per-action approval in a way that affects customers or cannot easily be reversed.
Customer-facing AI is high risk under this firm's model risk policy.
AI-generated content is published under the organisation's name.
Confidential or personal data is sent to an external model provider.
Can take actions that are hard to reverse.
Acts without approval of each individual action.

conditional_controls.reason: A human reviews every output at this autonomy level.
Every action needs human approval at L3.
The system can change state through tools.
Data is shared with an external model provider.
People outside the organisation encounter AI output.

controls.name: AI inventory registration
controls.description: Register the use case in the AI inventory with an accountable owner, tier and status.

controls.name: Periodic re-certification
controls.description: Repeat the gate review at the tier's cadence and after any material change.

controls.name: Approver sign-off
controls.description: Every approver role required for the tier signs before launch.

controls.name: Offline evaluation
controls.description: Held-out golden set at the tier's size and pass-rate minimums, with zero critical failures.

controls.name: Adversarial and red-team testing
controls.description: Prompt injection, jailbreak and abuse testing proportionate to exposure.

controls.name: Fairness evaluation
controls.description: Pass rates compared across relevant user segments, languages and dialects.
controls.evidence: Segment-level eval results and accepted gaps

controls.name: Continuous evaluation
controls.description: The eval suite runs on every prompt, model, retrieval or tool change and blocks releases below threshold.

controls.name: Human review of every output
controls.description: A person checks each output before it is used or sent.
controls.evidence: UX flow showing the review step

controls.name: Human approval of every action
controls.description: Each action is approved by a person before it executes.

controls.name: Sampled production review
controls.description: A weekly sample of production outputs is reviewed against the eval rubric.

controls.name: AI disclosure
controls.description: People are told when they are interacting with AI or reading AI-generated content.

controls.name: Explanation and contestability
controls.description: Affected people can get an explanation and ask for a human review of the outcome.

controls.name: Prompt-injection defences
controls.description: Retrieved, tool and user-supplied content is treated as untrusted data and cannot change goals or permissions.
controls.evidence: Design review and injection test results

controls.name: Least-privilege actions
controls.description: Tools are scoped to the task, with per-action and daily limits and confirmation for irreversible actions.
controls.evidence: Tool permission matrix and limits configuration

controls.name: Output handling
controls.description: Model output is sanitised before it is rendered, executed or passed to another system.

controls.name: Privacy review
controls.description: Privacy review or data protection impact assessment completed.

controls.name: Data minimisation and retention
controls.description: Only necessary data is sent; personal data is redacted from logs; retention limits are enforced.
controls.evidence: Data flow diagram and retention settings

controls.name: Vendor data terms
controls.description: Model vendor terms reviewed for training use, retention and residency.

controls.name: Permission-aware retrieval
controls.description: Users can only retrieve content they are entitled to see, enforced at query time.

controls.name: Monitoring and alerting
controls.description: Quality, safety, cost and latency are monitored with alert thresholds and owners.

controls.name: Kill switch and fallback
controls.description: The AI path can be switched off quickly, routing work to a tested non-AI fallback.
controls.evidence: Test record of the last switch-off

controls.name: Audit logging
controls.description: Inputs, outputs, decisions and approvals are logged with retention per policy.

controls.name: Incident runbook
controls.description: Runbook with AI-specific severities, containment steps and notification contacts.

controls.name: Model change management
controls.description: Exact model versions are pinned; any change is evaluated and rolled out like a release.

controls.name: Independent model validation
controls.description: Model risk management validates the model, data and monitoring before launch and annually.

incident_severities.description: Harmful, unlawful or data-exposing output reached users, or an unauthorised action executed.
incident_severities.response: Contain immediately with the kill switch or fallback; notify privacy, legal and security owners.

incident_severities.description: Systematic quality failure affecting many users, with no confirmed harm.
incident_severities.response: Fix within the agreed service level; consider pausing the rollout.
Log it, add the case to the eval set, fix in the normal cycle.
